summary:
Charter promotes a downloadable playbook from its sixth annual Charter Workplace Summit, held October 21 in New York. The event convened researchers, executives, and practitioners around the premise that leaders who pull ahead will both deploy AI ambitiously and sharpen distinctly human capabilities. Charter describes this as its largest summit to date, with more attendees and more sponsor support than prior years, and frames the sharing of ideas and insights as its primary measure of success.

At the summit, Charter launched the Charter AI Pulse, new research examining how AI is affecting the work and lives of more than 5,000 US desk workers who use AI. The playbook compiles the research's headline findings alongside top takeaways from every summit session, distilled into practical steps readers can apply immediately.

Content themes highlighted in the playbook include redesigning work around AI, developing managers who can lead both humans and AI agents, and making breaks part of the flow of work. The playbook also links to session videos. The post closes with a call to download the playbook, share it with colleagues, and attend future Charter summits.

The item is essentially promotional and contains little substantive detail beyond the research sample size, event date, and session topic list. It does not address workplace operations topics such as space booking, visitor management, attendance tracking, or facilities, focusing instead on AI adoption, management development, and worker wellbeing framing.
